description: A switched nonlinear RC: an ideal 5 V source, a latching switch (closed resistance 0.01 Ohm), a 10 kOhm resistor, a generic diode, and a 1 microfarad capacitor with an explicit initial voltage of 0 V, in series to ground. The switch starts open and is closed when step 5 is the newest, so it conducts from the end of step 4 (t = 4 ms, Stage 6 contract section 4.3). The reference integrates C dv/dt = i_D with i_D the diode current for (5 - v - v_D) / 10000.01 = i_D, by a fourth-order Runge-Kutta rule checked against half the step. The numbers are produced by tests/golden/stage-7-reference.py, which does not use the Engine; they are not Engine output.

expected.note: The last sample before the switch conducts is unchanged.

toleranceBasis: An independent emulation of the intended integration path (one backward-Euler step after the switch event, then the trapezoidal rule at 1 ms, with the diode solved exactly at each step) differs from the reference by about 0.05 mV at the three times; the reasoning that follows is why the tolerance is still 5 mV. At a 1 ms public step and a charging time constant of about 10 ms the trapezoidal rule's relative error is about (h / tau)^2 / 12 = 8e-4 of the change, which is below 4 mV of the 4.5 V change. The one backward-Euler step after the switch event adds about (h / tau)^2 / 2 = 0.5% of the change at that moment and decays with the circuit's time constant; at 50 ms (five time constants) it is below 0.4 mV. 5 mV covers both with margin. The tolerance is provisional: #109 and #111 may tighten it with evidence, and loosening it needs a contract change.

wrongVariants.name: diode reversed
wrongVariants.description: The diode's cathode is toward the resistor and its anode toward the capacitor. The capacitor charges only through the reverse leakage (1e-14 A plus 1e-12 S times the voltage across the diode), about 5 microvolts per second.
